projects.name: Ensuring refugee women and girls have access to GBV prevention and response services through mobile and static WGSS (Women and Girls Safe Spaces)
projects.description:
UNFPA's Women and Girls  Safe Spaces are crucial in supporting the Moldovan government's efforts to ensure that refugees have effective access to protection. By providing GBV response services and prevention interventions, UNFPA helps to protect vulnerable groups and create a safe environment where refugees are offered support to address protection concerns. The 11 UNFPA's Mobile Safe Spaces are operating across all rayons in Moldova, addressing the challenge of uneven access to protection services for refugees across different regions. By expanding the reach of these safe spaces through mobile units, UNFPA aims to close gaps in geographic coverage of protection services, particularly in rural or remote areas. This ensure that refugees, regardless of their location, have access to essential support and resources. The 20 Static Safe Spaces are located in strategic locations, including Border Crossing Points, Transit Points, and in RACs hosting the most vulnerable refugees, including Roma and persons with disabilities. 

To contribute to strengthened social cohesion and peaceful coexistence between refugee and host communities, UNFPA's Safe Spaces foster dialogue through recreational and non-formal education activities involving both refugees and host community members. This is particularly important for youth and adolescents, who can benefit from shared experiences and opportunities for interaction. By creating a welcoming and inclusive environment, Safe Spaces help to build bridges between different communities and promote understanding and tolerance.

To address the emotional distress that refugees in Moldova experience, the Safe Spaces offer a critical space where refugees and host community members can access individual and group psychosocial support. This support is essential for improving mental health and psychosocial well-being, helping individuals to cope with the challenges of displacement and rebuild their lives.

Considering the importance of coordination at the local level on protection-related developments and measurements, the Safe Spaces coordinate closely with Local Public Authorities to ensure a comprehensive and effective response to the needs of refugees in Moldova.

UNFPA will implement in 2024-2025 the integration of GBV prevention and response in medico-social centers located in Vulcanesti and Ocnita. The program aims to enhance the capacity of home care employees to address GBV among individuals with disabilities and older adults with limited mobility. Key activities include finalizing SOPs on GBV integration, continuing staff training, and continue establishing a safe reporting space for women with limited mobility.

projects.name: (UNFPA) Supporting Government with the perpetrators programs as part of the National Program for Preventing and Combating Violence Against Women and Girls and Domestic Violence 2023-2027
projects.description:
UNFPA will provide comprehensive support to the Government of the Republic of Moldova through targeted initiatives aimed at strengthening services for perpetrators of gender-based violence (GBV). This will include conducting a detailed analysis of existing services for perpetrators in Moldova, assessing the quality of current standards, and providing actionable recommendations for improvement. UNFPA will also support the development of a national concept for services targeting GBV perpetrators, including the revision and enhancement of existing national standards to ensure alignment with international best practices.

In collaboration with key government agencies, such as the probation, penitentiary, and police departments, UNFPA will assist in designing and adapting domestic violence rehabilitation programs. These programs will incorporate both early prevention measures and targeted interventions aimed at reducing recidivism and promoting behavioral change among perpetrators.

To ensure continuous improvement and accountability, UNFPA will develop a comprehensive evaluation framework to assess the effectiveness and impact of perpetrator rehabilitation programs. Furthermore, a high-level advocacy event will be organized to promote the implementation of Article 16 of the Istanbul Convention, emphasizing the importance of addressing and rehabilitating perpetrators as a critical component of preventing future violence.

Through these initiatives, UNFPA aims to enhance the national response to GBV, fostering a more comprehensive and effective approach to addressing the root causes of violence in Moldova.

During the period 2024–2025, the focus will be on strengthening the capacity of teachers delivering the Decisions for a Healthy Lifestyle course across all VET institutions by accrediting the continuous training program. Additionally, efforts will be made to equip schools with edutainment materials and menstrual hygiene products, as well as create a youth friendly learning classroom in 20 targeted VET institutions endowed with IT equipment.

Furthermore, support will be provided to strengthen the Peer Educators Network in promoting life skills education and increase the capacity of business companies from dual VET in creating a youth-friendly workplace. 

During 2025–2026, a dedicated training programme was also organized for nurses, psychologists and social pedagogues working in VET institutions to strengthen their capacity to support students’ well-being and healthy development.

During 2026–2027, a parenting programme will be developed and implemented to engage parents of VET students in supporting their children’s education and development. At the same time, Youth Centres will receive support in designing and implementing career guidance and employability skills programmes, helping young people strengthen the skills needed for their transition to the labour market.

The support will continue through 2027, with other strategic and system-wide interventions with support from the Austrian Development Agency.

projects.name: (UNFPA) Provision of cash assistance into GBV Case Management for survivors from refugee and host communities
projects.description:
As part of the Ukrainian Refugee Response in Moldova and to address GBV related risks, UNFPA has integrated cash assistance within GBV case management, targeting GBV survivors and individuals at risk of GBV – including Ukrainian refugees and vulnerable Moldovans. 
Strengthening the empowerment of women and girls via high quality CM&Cash support is the main reason the initiative is being undertaken. The programme has been informed by a thorough gender/GBV analysis  the analysis has influenced the
design of the programme.
The cash component of the GBV case management aims to empower survivors, mitigate GBV risks, and to support survivors in accessing GBV services by addressing the economic barriers that hinder survivors from escaping abusive situations and accessing life-saving GBV services. The cash element is integrated within the GBV CM in conjunction with other service components, such as psychosocial support, referral to other services, self-esteem strengthening, capacity building for economic independence and women’s rights. Prior to initiating the integration of cash assistance in GBV case management, a response analysis was conducted to determine situations when cash would be considered a useful and appropriate intervention based on context-specific analysis of GBV situations in Moldova. The response analysis resulted in a Response Framework outlining the precise contexts and situations in which cash is an appropriate assistance modality capable of responding to the GBV needs and risks of women and girls. The framework aims to support caseworkers in the assessment and selection process for cash assistance. Cash transfers to bank accounts have been deemed the most appropriate cash delivery mechanism. The cash transfer value is calculated based on the vulnerability and need of each individual as per the case plan. A monitoring framework has been established to ensure a regular and systematic process of data collection and analysis of the integration of Cash in GBV case management. The purpose of the monitoring is to collect feedback that can improve the implementation of cash assistance in the case management process, and track its risks and benefits, in order to create better protection outcomes for survivors and individuals at risk of GBV. The monitoring framework includes different tools. Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) surveys will be administered by the case worker to gather information from the survivors using a questionnaire. This information will be triangulated with data gathered from the Complaint and Feedback Mechanism (CFM). Output monitoring has been conducted to monitor the programme outreach, including the number of individuals reached with cash assistance interventions and the total value transferred directly to individuals for cash assistance. The monitoring includes disaggregated information on gender, age, disability, displacement status, number of dependents of survivors, number of installments, and delivery mechanism to enable regular trend analysis of the cash distribution. 
Process monitoring is conducted through the PDM surveys and monitoring of CFM, aimed to monitor the cash assistance distribution process to be able to capture any factors that may affect the quality, safety, and access of survivors to the cash assistance. The PDM surveys aim to capture whether the survivors deem the duration, timing, and amount of the cash assistance to be adequate to improve their safety, and whether the survivors were able to access cash assistance safely.

projects.name: Out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education for youth, including young people with disabilities, is operationalized following international standards.
projects.description:
To complement the formal/school-based comprehensive sexuality education and reach out to adolescents and youth from vulnerable groups and remote areas, UNFPA has been supporting for many years the out-of-school programs. 
In 2023 UNFPA will continue implementing the out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) program. This initiative will follow UNFPA’s International Technical and Programmatic Guidance on Out-of-School CSE and will focus on reaching adolescents and young people in rural areas, those with disabilities, and youth from the left bank of the Nistru River.
In 2024, the initiative aims to foster a more inclusive and supportive environment where all young people, regardless of their background, have access to comprehensive sexuality education and essential resources for a healthy and informed future. To achieve this, several institutions and organizations working with youth will be equipped with dedicated spaces for non-formal sexuality education activities.
Additionally, civil society organizations, particularly those in underserved regions, will receive support to enhance their capacity in promoting young people’s sexual and reproductive health and rights. Specialists from various organizations will be trained to deliver accurate, age-appropriate education on these topics, ensuring that young people are well-informed and empowered.
Furthermore, parents and caregivers of adolescents with disabilities will be provided with the necessary knowledge and resources to support their children’s development and smooth transition into adulthood.
In 2025, UNFPA will continue strengthening civil society organizations and youth networks across Moldova, including those on the left bank of the Nistru River, to develop and implement programs on sexual and reproductive health and rights tailored to diverse youth groups. To support these efforts, UNFPA will create guidelines for delivering youth-friendly health services for vulnerable youth, aligned with international out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (OOS CSE) standards.
A digital training program will be introduced for facilitators working in CSE, ensuring they are well-equipped to provide accurate and effective education. Additionally, new educational and interactive materials, such as the Diary of an Adolescent Boy/Girl, will be developed to make information on sexual and reproductive health and rights more accessible and relevant to young people. 
Building on UNFPA Moldova’s expertise in youth well-being and global best practices, and in partnership with the Ministry of Education and Research (MER) and the Youth National Agency, UNFPA will establish the Future-Ready Hub—a pioneering space dedicated to life skills development, innovation, and modern technologies. Bringing together adolescents, youth educators, youth workers, NGOs, and the private sector, the Hub will foster a collaborative, forward-looking environment. 

In 2026, UNFPA will continue supporting NGOs to deliver out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) programmes for adolescents and young people. Organizations trained in previous years will receive further support to reach adolescents with disabilities and those from rural areas or families affected by poverty, violence, and other vulnerabilities. NGOs will also be supported to integrate the Adolescent Diary into their programmes, both as a complementary resource and as a stand-alone CSE tool.
Healthcare providers from the left bank of the Nistru River will receive continuous supervision on specific health and CSE topics to strengthen their capacity to provide accurate, evidence-based, and youth-friendly medical and psychological services. In addition, they will be empowered and supported to act as trainers for local school staff.
As part of the operationalisation of the EduLIFE Hub, planned for launch this year, a regionally co-created curriculum and handbook on life skills will be developed. These resources will support educators in strengthening adolescents’ competencies in sexuality education and in developing the skills necessary to navigate modern societies.
Additionally, UNFPA will conduct a national youth-centered campaign to promote healthy and safe adolescent development, including targeted messages on the prevention of teenage pregnancy.

projects.name: (UNFPA) Strengthened capacity of the General Education system to deliver quality health education and create an enabling environment for students’ wellbeing and healthy development.
projects.description:
As part of its ongoing commitment to the Ministry of Education and Research (MER), UNFPA continues to enhance national capacity and policy in the education sector, empowering pupils and youth through life-skills development and supporting their safe transition to adulthood. UNFPA will provide sustained technical expertise to advance national priorities related to adolescent and youth well-being, comprehensive sexuality education (CSE), and safe and healthy development. Additionally, it will support MER in strengthening communication and promoting the roles of schools and families in education. 
In 2023, is formalising its collaboration with the Ministry of Education and Research by signing a Memorandum of Understanding for the 2023-2027 period. 
Following the International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education and addressing national needs, UNFPA will support the Ministry in developing a health education school club for grades V-VII. In 2023, the curriculum and didactic resources will be developed, with pilot implementation and finalization planned for 2024. 
Additionally, UNFPA will piloted the EduLIFE School Program: friendly environment, access to health education, and menstrual hygiene products. This concept embodies a multidimensional approach to strengthening the educational institutions’ ability to contribute to students' well-being and life skills, encouraging healthy and non-violent behaviour, promoting equal learning opportunities for both girls and boy
In 2024, UNFPA is expanding the "EduLIFE School" model to four new schools, including two designated as Model Schools. This initiative will promote a student-friendly environment, comprehensive sexuality education, and access to menstrual hygiene products. The selection of schools will be carried out in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, with two institutions being reorganized to accommodate refugee students from Ukraine. Key implementing partners will include the NGO “Youth Media Center” and the platform “suntparinte.md.”
In 2025, alongside with other UN agencies, UNFPA is assisting MER in conducting a national school survey among pupils, parents, and teachers. The survey will assess education quality, student participation, informal payments, rights awareness, gender equality, bullying, well-being, and include dedicated questions on CSE. 
As one of the key partners in the National Curriculum reform, UNFPA is building the capacities of curriculum authors to evaluate the existing curriculum and develop a new one. International standards and assessment tools in CSE will guide this process, ensuring the integration of CSE and life-skills topics into the new mandatory national curriculum. 

UNFPA will also support MER in organizing Education Week in May 2025, contributing to organization of a national conference with local and regional education experts and organizing a side event on Dual Education in the Vocational Education and Training (VET) system. 
Building on 2024 achievements, UNFPA will pilot a curriculum-based school club on health education, providing training and continuous support to 30 teachers from various schools. 

In 2026, UNFPA will continue to support the integration of health education, including comprehensive sexuality education (CSE), into the formal curriculum as part of the national curriculum reform. The working group responsible for the subject Me and Society will receive technical support to integrate these topics while developing the key curricular products, including the conceptual framework, the curriculum, and the methodological guide for teachers. Once these materials are finalized, UNFPA will begin delivering a long-term in-service capacity-building programme for the first cohort of Me and Society teachers who will start implementing the curriculum in September 2027.

Additionally, UNFPA will continue to provide technical support to MER in the process of institutionalizing the menstrual health and hygiene programme. As part of this process, UNFPA will conduct an assessment of the use of public funds by schools during the 2026–2027 school year and the actual access of girls to menstrual pads. The findings will inform the design of the fund disbursement process for the resources already allocated by MER for the 2027–2028 school year.

Building on the experience of previous years in supporting parents of adolescents to strengthen their knowledge of health and sexuality education topics—enabling them to better support the healthy development of their children—and in line with MER’s initiative to develop an ecosystem of parenting programmes, UNFPA will provide technical support for the development of a legal framework on parenting and will pilot a parenting programme.

Following the School Barometer research conducted last year, UNFPA will support a communication campaign to disseminate the findings. The organization will also support the National Pupils’ Council to share the results with their peers, consult them on recommendations and solutions, and present these during Education Week.

Finally, UNFPA will contribute to the collection of data on health behaviours among school-aged children through the HBSC study, in order to inform evidence-based decision-making in the education and health sectors.

projects.description: The project aims to enhance shared prosperity in Moldova by 2028, ensuring that women and girls, especially the most vulnerable, including NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) women, will benefit from family friendly opportunities and sustainable economic development, including access to gender-responsive workplaces and employment. It targets local government institutions, professional training providers, and private sector representatives. The project will target women and girls from 5 rayons, including Chisinau, and the number of beneficiaries is estimated from the average demographic statistics, as the exact rayons of work will be determined later during the assessment.  An average rayon population (excluding Chisinau and UTA Gagauzia) is about  50,000 people, with women above 50%, and out of these, less than 20% are women and girls 15-64 years old. It will encompass study assessments, capacity building, developing and piloting inclusive employment measures, extending childcare services, and promoting FFP. The project will also raise awareness and share best practices to ensure sustainable impact. This holistic approach addresses socio-economic challenges, aiming to create a more inclusive and equitable labour market in Moldova, ultimately contributing to the country's sustainable economic development and the well-being of its diverse population.

projects.name: Enhancing the effectiveness of labour market institutions in the Republic of Moldova to design and implement inclusive policies that generate quality jobs, promote fair working conditions, and safeguard workers’ rights.
projects.description:
The overall objective of the project is to improve access to more and better employment opportunities in the Republic of Moldova.
Specific Objectives / Outcomes: 
- Strengthened capacity of the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MoLSP) and the National Employment Agency (NEA) to prevent and address labour market exclusion.
-Enhanced capacity of the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MoLSP) and the State Labour Inspectorate (SLI) to improve working conditions and ensure the protection of workers’ rights.
Objective 1: focuses on improving the institutional capacity of the MoLSP and NEA to deliver on the objectives of the national employment policy framework. This will be achieved through diversifying employment services and programmes expanding individualized service delivery, strengthening the performance management system, improving the in-house training system for NEA staff, including modernization of a new office for NEA staff in Cimislia.
Objective 2: aims to reinforce the capacity of the SLI to fulfil its state control mandate. This will be achieved by reviewing and updating legal frameworks and internal policies, planning inspection visits more strategically, improving the training system for SLI staff, modernizing procedures and upgrading the SLI information system, strengthening collaboration with social partners, providing necessary material and logistical support, including modernization of a new office for SLI staff in MoLSP premises.
projects.outcome: OU 3.1_Policy and institutional frameworks create an empowering environment for inclusive and sustainable economic development that promotes creation of productive and decent work
